newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Nedlloyd Q3 profits.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Nedlloyd Q3 profits.

text.p: Dutch shipping and transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Group NV NYLN.AS said on Wednesday its third quarter net profit from ordinary operations fell to 38 million guilders from 63 million in the same period in 1995.
Roel Gooskens, analyst at Van Meer James Capel
"The net is a little above expectations, but the future looks mediocre to me. They repeat they expect 1996 results to be modestly positive, so the fourth quarter will be less good."

"If they include the proceeds of the sales of Smit Internationale (some tens of millions) in these expectations, the fourth quarter is to really disappoint. It all depends on how the cooperation with P&O will work out. We maintain it a sell."
Oscar Poos, Dutch analyst at Paribas Capital Markets

"The bottom line was higher than I had been expecting. I was going for 26 million guilders. Shipping is improving more than I expected. But the recovery in Germany is going more slowly than I expected. Their forecast is quite modest for this year. I was going for a small profit. There was no statement about 1997. 1997 may be worse and 1998 may be the bottom of the cycle. Container shipping is not a (good) business to be in. I have a neutral opinion on the company. I am probably going to switch to sell again. But I haven't decided about that."
